What is the realistic path to fleet-scale unit economics, and which deployment scenarios (logistics, manufacturing, services) are most likely to reach commercial viability first within 3–5 years?
How do safety certification and regulatory frameworks in major markets (US, EU, Asia) constrain or shape the deployment timeline?

sources.title: Teleoperation of Humanoid Robots: A Survey
sources.abstract: Teleoperation of humanoid robots enables the integration of the cognitive skills and domain expertise of humans with the physical capabilities of humanoid robots. The operational versatility of humanoid robots makes them the ideal platform for a wide range of applications when teleoperating in a remote environment. However, the complexity of humanoid robots imposes challenges for teleoperation, particularly in unstructured dynamic environments with limited communication. Many advancements have been achieved in the last decades in this area, but a comprehensive overview is still missing. This survey article gives an extensive overview of humanoid robot teleoperation, presenting the general architecture of a teleoperation system and analyzing the different components. We also discuss different aspects of the topic, including technological and methodological advances, as well as potential applications.

sources.title: iRonCub 3: The Jet-Powered Flying Humanoid Robot
sources.abstract: This article presents iRonCub 3, a jet-powered humanoid robot, and its first flight experiments. Unlike traditional aerial vehicles, iRonCub 3 aims to achieve flight using a full-body humanoid form, which poses unique challenges in control, estimation, and system integration. We highlight the robot's current mechanical and software architecture, including its propulsion system, control framework, and experimental infrastructure. The control and estimation framework is first validated in simulation by performing a takeoff and tracking a reference trajectory. Then, we demonstrate, for the first time, a liftoff of a jet-powered humanoid robot - an initial but significant step toward aerial humanoid mobility. Also, we detail how the experimental area around a jet-powered humanoid robot should be designed in order to deal with a level of complexity that is substantially superior than indoor humanoid robot experiments.

sources.title: Expressive Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Robots
sources.abstract: Can we enable humanoid robots to generate rich, diverse, and expressive motions in the real world? We propose to learn a whole-body control policy on a human-sized robot to mimic human motions as realistic as possible. To train such a policy, we leverage the large-scale human motion capture data from the graphics community in a Reinforcement Learning framework. However, directly performing imitation learning with the motion capture dataset would not work on the real humanoid robot, given the large gap in degrees of freedom and physical capabilities. Our method Expressive Whole-Body Control (Exbody) tackles this problem by encouraging the upper humanoid body to imitate a reference motion, while relaxing the imitation constraint on its two legs and only requiring them to follow a given velocity robustly. With training in simulation and Sim2Real transfer, our policy can control a humanoid robot to walk in different styles, shake hands with humans, and even dance with a human in the real world. We conduct extensive studies and comparisons on diverse motions in both simulation and the real world to show the effectiveness of our approach.

sources.title: Whole-body Humanoid Robot Locomotion with Human Reference
sources.abstract: Recently, humanoid robots have made significant advances in their ability to perform challenging tasks due to the deployment of Reinforcement Learning (RL), however, the inherent complexity of humanoid robots, including the difficulty of designing complicated reward functions and training entire sophisticated systems, still poses a notable challenge. To conquer these challenges, after many iterations and in-depth investigations, we have meticulously developed a full-size humanoid robot, "Adam", whose innovative structural design greatly improves the efficiency and effectiveness of the imitation learning process. In addition, we have developed a novel imitation learning framework based on an adversarial motion prior, which applies not only to Adam but also to humanoid robots in general. Using the framework, Adam can exhibit unprecedented human-like characteristics in locomotion tasks. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables Adam to achieve human-comparable performance in complex locomotion tasks, marking the first time that human locomotion data has been used for imitation learning in a full-size humanoid robot.

sources.title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
sources.abstract: General-purpose robots need a versatile body and an intelligent mind. Recent advancements in humanoid robots have shown great promise as a hardware platform for building generalist autonomy in the human world. A robot foundation model, trained on massive and diverse data sources, is essential for enabling the robots to reason about novel situations, robustly handle real-world variability, and rapidly learn new tasks. To this end, we introduce GR00T N1, an open foundation model for humanoid robots. GR00T N1 is a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model with a dual-system architecture. The vision-language module (System 2) interprets the environment through vision and language instructions. The subsequent diffusion transformer module (System 1) generates fluid motor actions in real time. Both modules are tightly coupled and jointly trained end-to-end. We train GR00T N1 with a heterogeneous mixture of real-robot trajectories, human videos, and synthetically generated datasets. We show that our generalist robot model GR00T N1 outperforms the state-of-the-art imitation learning baselines on standard simulation benchmarks across multiple robot embodiments. Furthermore, we deploy our model on the Fourier GR-1 humanoid robot for language-conditioned bimanual manipulation tasks, achieving strong performance with high data efficiency.

sources.title: MASH: Cooperative-Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Single Humanoid Robot Locomotion
sources.abstract: This paper proposes a novel method to enhance locomotion for a single humanoid robot through cooperative-heterogeneous multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL). While most existing methods typically employ single-agent reinforcement learning algorithms for a single humanoid robot or MARL algorithms for multi-robot system tasks, we propose a distinct paradigm: applying cooperative-heterogeneous MARL to optimize locomotion for a single humanoid robot. The proposed method, multi-agent reinforcement learning for single humanoid locomotion (MASH), treats each limb (legs and arms) as an independent agent that explores the robot's action space while sharing a global critic for cooperative learning. Experiments demonstrate that MASH accelerates training convergence and improves whole-body cooperation ability, outperforming conventional single-agent reinforcement learning methods. This work advances the integration of MARL into single-humanoid-robot control, offering new insights into efficient locomotion strategies.

sources.title: Advancements in Humanoid Robots: A Comprehensive Review and Future Prospects
sources.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive review of the current status, advancements, and future prospects of humanoid robots, highlighting their significance in driving the evolution of next-generation industries. By analyzing various research endeavors and key technologies, encompassing ontology structure, control and decision-making, and perception and interaction, a holistic overview of the current state of humanoid robot research is presented. Furthermore, emerging challenges in the field are identified, emphasizing the necessity for a deeper understanding of biological motion mechanisms, improved structural design, enhanced material applications, advanced drive and control methods, and efficient energy utilization. The integration of bionics, brain-inspired intelligence, mechanics, and control is underscored as a promising direction for the development of advanced humanoid robotic systems. This paper serves as an invaluable resource, offering insightful guidance to researchers in the field, while contributing to the ongoing evolution and potential of humanoid robots across diverse domains.

sources.title: Perception for Humanoid Robots
sources.abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review The field of humanoid robotics, perception plays a fundamental role in enabling robots to interact seamlessly with humans and their surroundings, leading to improved safety, efficiency, and user experience. This scientific study investigates various perception modalities and techniques employed in humanoid robots, including visual, auditory, and tactile sensing by exploring recent state-of-the-art approaches for perceiving and understanding the internal state, the environment, objects, and human activities. Recent Findings Internal state estimation makes extensive use of Bayesian filtering methods and optimization techniques based on maximum a-posteriori formulation by utilizing proprioceptive sensing. In the area of external environment understanding, with an emphasis on robustness and adaptability to dynamic, unforeseen environmental changes, the new slew of research discussed in this study have focused largely on multi-sensor fusion and machine learning in contrast to the use of hand-crafted, rule-based systems. Human robot interaction methods have established the importance of contextual information representation and memory for understanding human intentions. Summary This review summarizes the recent developments and trends in the field of perception in humanoid robots. Three main areas of application are identified, namely, internal state estimation, external environment estimation, and human robot interaction. The applications of diverse sensor modalities in each of these areas are considered and recent significant works are discussed.

sources.title: LiPS: Large-Scale Humanoid Robot Reinforcement Learning with Parallel-Series Structures
sources.abstract: In recent years, research on humanoid robots has garnered significant attention, particularly in reinforcement learning based control algorithms, which have achieved major breakthroughs. Compared to traditional model-based control algorithms, reinforcement learning based algorithms demonstrate substantial advantages in handling complex tasks. Leveraging the large-scale parallel computing capabilities of GPUs, contemporary humanoid robots can undergo extensive parallel training in simulated environments. A physical simulation platform capable of large-scale parallel training is crucial for the development of humanoid robots. As one of the most complex robot forms, humanoid robots typically possess intricate mechanical structures, encompassing numerous series and parallel mechanisms. However, many reinforcement learning based humanoid robot control algorithms currently employ open-loop topologies during training, deferring the conversion to series-parallel structures until the sim2real phase. This approach is primarily due to the limitations of physics engines, as current GPU-based physics engines often only support open-loop topologies or have limited capabilities in simulating multi-rigid-body closed-loop topologies. For enabling reinforcement learning-based humanoid robot control algorithms to train in large-scale parallel environments, we propose a novel training method LiPS. By incorporating multi-rigid-body dynamics modeling in the simulation environment, we significantly reduce the sim2real gap and the difficulty of converting to parallel structures during model deployment, thereby robustly supporting large-scale reinforcement learning for humanoid robots.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Review of Humanoid Robots
sources.abstract: ABSTRACT Humanoid robots, increasingly recognized for their potential to drive economic and social development, have garnered significant attention in recent years. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the progress, challenges, and future directions in humanoid robotics, with a particular emphasis on essential system components and key technological innovations. Through a review of historical milestones, this paper explores critical aspects such as the design of the head and body, and examines state‐of‐the‐art technologies in areas like locomotion control, perception, and intelligent manipulation. By presenting a thorough analysis of the field, this work aims to serve as a valuable resource for researchers and inspire future innovations that will drive the continued evolution of humanoid robots.

sources.title: Trinity: A Modular Humanoid Robot AI System
sources.abstract: In recent years, research on humanoid robots has garnered increasing attention. With breakthroughs in various types of artificial intelligence algorithms, embodied intelligence, exemplified by humanoid robots, has been highly anticipated. The advancements in reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms have significantly improved the motion control and generalization capabilities of humanoid robots. Simultaneously, the groundbreaking progress in large language models (LLM) and visual language models (VLM) has brought more possibilities and imagination to humanoid robots. LLM enables humanoid robots to understand complex tasks from language instructions and perform long-term task planning, while VLM greatly enhances the robots' understanding and interaction with their environment. This paper introduces \textcolor{magenta}{Trinity}, a novel AI system for humanoid robots that integrates RL, LLM, and VLM. By combining these technologies, Trinity enables efficient control of humanoid robots in complex environments. This innovative approach not only enhances the capabilities but also opens new avenues for future research and applications of humanoid robotics.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots and Humanoid AI: Review, Perspectives and Directions
sources.abstract: In the approximately century-long journey of robotics, humanoid robots made their debut around six decades ago. The rapid advancements in generative AI, large language models (LLMs), and large multimodal models (LMMs) have reignited interest in humanoids, steering them towards real-time, interactive, and multimodal designs and applications. This resurgence unveils boundless opportunities for AI robotics and novel applications, paving the way for automated, real-time and humane interactions with humanoid advisers, educators, medical professionals, caregivers, and receptionists. However, while current humanoid robots boast humanlike appearances, they have yet to embody true humaneness, remaining distant from achieving human-like intelligence. In our comprehensive review, we delve into the intricate landscape of AI robotics and AI humanoid robots in particular, exploring the challenges, perspectives and directions in transitioning from human-looking to humane humanoids and fostering human-like robotics. This endeavour synergizes the advancements in LLMs, LMMs, generative AI, and human-level AI with humanoid robotics, omniverse, and decentralized AI, ushering in the era of AI humanoids and humanoid AI.

sources.title: iWalker: Imperative Visual Planning for Walking Humanoid Robot
sources.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), 2025
sources.abstract: Humanoid robots, designed to operate in human-centric environments, serve as a fundamental platform for a broad range of tasks. Although humanoid robots have been extensively studied for decades, a majority of existing humanoid robots still heavily rely on complex modular frameworks, leading to inflexibility and potential compounded errors from independent sensing, planning, and acting components. In response, we propose an end-to-end humanoid sense-plan-act walking system, enabling vision-based obstacle avoidance and footstep planning for whole body balancing simultaneously. We designed two imperative learning (IL)-based bilevel optimizations for model-predictive step planning and whole body balancing, respectively, to achieve self-supervised learning for humanoid robot walking. This enables the robot to learn from arbitrary unlabeled data, improving its adaptability and generalization capabilities. We refer to our method as iWalker and demonstrate its effectiveness in both simulated and real-world environments, representing a significant advancement toward autonomous humanoid robots.

sources.title: The Cybersecurity of a Humanoid Robot
sources.abstract: The rapid advancement of humanoid robotics presents unprecedented cybersecurity challenges that existing theoretical frameworks fail to adequately address. This report presents a comprehensive security assessment of a production humanoid robot platform, bridging the gap between abstract security models and operational vulnerabilities. Through systematic static analysis, runtime observation, and cryptographic examination, we uncovered a complex security landscape characterized by both sophisticated defensive mechanisms and critical vulnerabilities. Our findings reveal a dual-layer proprietary encryption system (designated FMX') that, while innovative in design, suffers from fundamental implementation flaws including the use of static cryptographic keys that enable offline configuration decryption. More significantly, we documented persistent telemetry connections transmitting detailed robot state information--including audio, visual, spatial, and actuator data--to external servers without explicit user consent or notification mechanisms. We operationalized a Cybersecurity AI agent on the Unitree G1 to map and prepare exploitation of its manufacturer's cloud infrastructure, illustrating how a compromised humanoid can escalate from covert data collection to active counter-offensive operations. We argue that securing humanoid robots requires a paradigm shift toward Cybersecurity AI (CAI) frameworks that can adapt to the unique challenges of physical-cyber convergence. This work contributes empirical evidence for developing robust security standards as humanoid robots transition from research curiosities to operational systems in critical domains.

sources.title: Intelligent Humanoid Robots in Manufacturing
sources.venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction (HRI)
sources.abstract: Technological evolution in the field of robotics is emerging with major breakthroughs in recent years. This was especially fostered by revolutionary new software applications leading to humanoid robots. Humanoids are being envisioned for manufacturing applications to form human-robot teams. But their implication in the manufacturing practices especially for industrial safety standards and lean manufacturing practices have been minimally addressed. Humanoids will also be competing with conventional robotic arms and effective methods to assess their return on investment are needed. To study the next generation of industrial automation, we used the case context of Tesla's humanoid robot. The company has recently unveiled its project on an intelligent humanoid robot named 'Optimus' to achieve an increased level of manufacturing automation. This article proposes a framework to integrate humanoids for manufacturing automation and also presents the significance of safety standards of human-robot collaboration. A case of lean assembly cell for the manufacturing of an open-source medical ventilator was used for human-humanoid automation. Simulation results indicate that humanoids can increase the level of manufacturing automation. Managerial and research implications are presented.

sources.title: Perception-and-action system for humanoid robot task execution in construction
sources.venue: Computer-Aided Civil and Infrastructure Engineering, Volume 50, 100107, ISSN 1093-9687, 2026
sources.abstract: Humanoid robots, with their human-like shape and multi-tasking capabilities, are well-aligned with human-dominated workplaces, like those in civil and construction engineering, where they could collaborate with human workers or autonomously perform physically demanding and hazardous tasks. Despite this promise, limited research has explored how to endow these robots with the practical capabilities needed to perform construction tasks. To this end, this study proposes a novel perception-and-action system that enables humanoid robots to learn and perform construction tasks from worker demonstrations. This system contains two deep networks: Humanoid-PoseNet, which extracts human postures and translates them into mechanically feasible poses for a humanoid robot; and Humanoid-ActionNet, which learns robot-executable actions based on these translated poses. Experimental results demonstrate that the humanoid robot reliably executed eight construction-related actions, achieving an average motion-tracking error of 82.45 mm MPJPE (Mean Per Joint Position Error). This work provides an early step toward deploying humanoid collaborators in construction.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots and Humanoid AI: Review, Perspectives and Directions
sources.abstract: In the approximately century-long journey of robotics, humanoid robots made their debut around six decades ago. The rapid advancements in generative AI, large language models (LLMs), and large multimodal models (LMMs) have reignited interest in humanoids, steering them towards real-time, interactive, and multimodal designs and applications. This resurgence unveils boundless opportunities for AI robotics and novel applications, paving the way for automated, real-time and humane interactions with humanoid advisers, educators, medical professionals, caregivers, and receptionists. However, while current humanoid robots boast humanlike appearances, they have yet to embody true humaneness, remaining distant from achieving human-like intelligence. In our comprehensive review, we delve into the intricate landscape of AI robotics and AI humanoid robots in particular, exploring the challenges, perspectives and directions in transitioning from human-looking to humane humanoids and fostering human-like robotics. This endeavour synergizes the advancements in LLMs, LMMs, generative AI, and human-level AI with humanoid robotics, omniverse, and decentralized AI, ushering in the era of AI humanoids and humanoid AI.

sources.title: Reliability-Based Preventive Maintenance for a Humanoid Robot System Under Dependent Competing Failure Processes
sources.abstract: Modeling system reliability under dependent competing failure processes remains challenging due to the complex interactions among failure modes. In such systems, soft failures arise from the combined effects of continuous degradation and additional damage induced by abrupt external shocks, while hard failures are triggered by sudden and catastrophic stresses from the same shock process. In this work, a general reliability model is developed by incorporating coupling factors, permitting a formulation that is independent of specific degradation or shock models and does not rely on predefined failure mode classifications. Then, a tailored solution algorithm is designed for the proposed reliability model by decoupling the originally coupled structure and incorporating auxiliary variables and additional constraints. Building on this framework, a preventive maintenance strategy is developed to minimize the average long-run cost rate under periodic inspection. Finally, the reliability model and maintenance approach are implemented on a humanoid robot system, demonstrating the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

sources.title: Self-Healing Action Verification against Instruction Tampering and Sensor Failures in Humanoid Robots
sources.abstract: As humanoid robots are increasingly used in complex real-world environments, reliable verification of robot actions becomes more important. Action verification should not only check whether the executed action matches the intended instruction, but also keep reliable performance when motor-sensor observations are affected by failures. Traditional instruction authentication mainly protects the instruction itself and cannot directly verify the final physical action of the robot. In addition, the sensing information used to observe robot execution may also become unreliable. In this paper, we propose a self-healing motor-based action verification framework that combines explainable sensor selection, temporal masked reconstruction, and multiscale action recognition. First, Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) are used to identify motor encoders that provide important information for action discrimination. Then, the selected encoder signals are processed by a temporal masked reconstruction model to recover unreliable joint observations based on temporal continuity and cross-joint coordination. After that, a multiscale gallery recognizer with zero trainable classifier parameters is used to infer the physical action executed by the robot. The inferred action is finally compared with the trusted intended instruction to detect instruction-execution inconsistency. The proposed framework is evaluated on a Booster Robotics K1 Education humanoid robot under multiple sensor-failure modes and different corruption levels, and is compared with several existing methods. The proposed method achieves average accuracies of 98.4% and 94.8% for single-action and compound-action recognition, respectively. Under different sensor-failure levels, the proposed self-healing method achieves an average recognition accuracy of 92.6%.

sources.title: The Humanoid Illusion (v2.0): The Missing Unified Operator in Humanoid Robotics and the Industry-10.0 Framework
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: Humanoid robotics accelerated substantially between 2024 and 2026 through the integration of multimodal reasoning models, robot foundation models, large scale teleoperation datasets, and Vision Language–Action (VLA) architectures. These systems create the appearance of general purpose physical intelligence through increasingly capable behavioral coordination across perception, planning, and control layers. This paper argues that such systems remain fundamentally stacked architectures ratherthan unified agents. Contemporary humanoids combine latent semantic reasoning, probabilistic world models, teleoperation derived priors, deterministic control systems, and heuristic safety wrappers, but do not implement a monadically coherent grounding framework unifying semantic structure, physical dynamics, stochastic uncertainty, and safety invariants within a single constraint-preserving operator. We formalize unified agency through the criterionUnified Agency ⇐⇒ D(S,W,C,A),where semantics S, world state W, constraints C, and actions A participate in a unified decision operator preserving representational and physical coherence. The paper develops a categorical grounding framework based on typed state spaces, distributive monadic lifting, and constraint preserving grounding functors between semantic and physical domains. Within this framework, empirical humanoid failure modes including distribution shift instability, inconsistent affordance grounding, teleoperation overfit ting, and safety violations are interpreted as failures of grounding coherence between latent semanticrepresentations and typed physical realizations. The paper further introduces Industry–10, a minimal structural specification class for coherent embodied agency based on typed semantic grounding, invariant preserving physical realization, and unifiedcognitive physical control. The framework provides a computable formalization of grounding coherence for embodied intelligence and a diagnostic basis for evaluating contemporary humanoid architectures..

sources.title: Time-to-Fault Prediction Framework for Automated Manufacturing in Humanoid Robotics Using Deep Learning
sources.abstract: Industry 4.0 is transforming predictive failure management by utilizing deep learning to enhance maintenance strategies and automate production processes. Traditional methods often fail to predict failures in time. This research addresses this issue by developing a time-to-fault prediction framework that utilizes an enhanced long short-term memory (LSTM) model to predict machine faults. The proposed method integrates real-time sensor data, including current, voltage, and temperature calibrated via ultra-sensitive optical sensing technologies based on the typical whispering gallery optical mode (WGM) to create a robust dataset. Due to the high-quality factor that these sensors exhibit, any minute change on the surrounding medium will makes a significant change on its transmission spectrum. The LSTM model trained on these data demonstrated rapid and stable convergence, outperforming other deep learning techniques with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.83, a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 1.62, and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.99. The results show the superior performance of LSTM in predicting machine failures early in real-world environments within 10 min lead time, improving productivity and reducing downtime. This framework advances smart industries by improving fault prediction in manufacturing precision robotics components, demonstrated through two humanoid robots, GUCnoid 1.0 and ARAtronica.

sources.title: Coherence Loss in Humanoid Robotics A Triad-Based Diagnostic Interpretation
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: 04-26-2026: The frameworks and concepts originate from the author's observation and pattern recognition. Large language models served as articulation and stress-testing tools throughout development. No changes made aside from the addition of this disclosure. This working paper applies the Coherence (C), Boundary Transfer (L), and Regime Margin (R) triad from the Emergent Order Systems (EOS) framework to the documented engineering challenges of humanoid robotics, focusing on motion control as an openly acknowledged unsolved problem in the field. The paper argues that the primary failure modes — sensor fusion degradation, model-DOF mismatch, and real-time feedback bandwidth limits — share a common underlying structure expressible as coherence loss across interconnected subsystems. Drawing on a published bridge layer from virtual and augmented reality coherence analysis, where structural isomorphism between VR/AR and autonomous system failure modes has been established, the triad is mapped to humanoid subsystem failure modes as a substrate-independent diagnostic language. The contribution is descriptive and non-prescriptive: no control algorithms or safety architectures are proposed.

sources.title: A Novel Risk Assessment Framework for Ensuring the Safety of Humanoid Robots
sources.venue: Journal of Institute of Control Robotics and Systems
sources.abstract: Humanoid robots mimic human forms and utilize advanced artificial intelligence (AI), creating complex safety challenges that traditional frameworks struggle to address. This paper proposes an integrated risk assessment framework tailored for humanoid robots, combining Failure Modes and Effects Analysis, System-Theoretic Process Analysis, and an AI-specific Risk Index. Additionally, it systematically identifies and evaluates risks from mechanical and electrical failures, control system errors, and AI-driven behaviors such as biased data handling and unpredictable real-time decision-making. Applying this framework to 30 risk scenarios revealed critical vulnerabilities, including power system malfunctions, software logic errors, and autonomous decision anomalies. Based on these findings, specific safety measures were developed, emphasizing redundant hardware controls, multi-sensor validation, real-time software monitoring, and robust fail-safe mechanisms. The integrated approach significantly enhances traditional risk assessments, effectively bridging the gap between existing robotics safety standards and new AI-driven challenges, ensuring the safe and reliable operation of humanoid robots in dynamic human environments.

sources.title: Humanoid Manipulation Interface: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Robot-Free Demonstrations
sources.abstract: Current approaches for humanoid whole-body manipulation, primarily relying on teleoperation or visual sim-to-real reinforcement learning, are hindered by hardware logistics and complex reward engineering. Consequently, demonstrated autonomous skills remain limited and are typically restricted to controlled environments. In this paper, we present the Humanoid Manipulation Interface (HuMI), a portable and efficient framework for learning diverse whole-body manipulation tasks across various environments. HuMI enables robot-free data collection by capturing rich whole-body motion using portable hardware. This data drives a hierarchical learning pipeline that translates human motions into dexterous and feasible humanoid skills. Extensive experiments across five whole-body tasks--including kneeling, squatting, tossing, walking, and bimanual manipulation--demonstrate that HuMI achieves a 3x increase in data collection efficiency compared to teleoperation and attains a 70% success rate in unseen environments.

findings.claim: A scenario-based risk assessment of humanoid robots found critical vulnerabilities in power systems, software logic and autonomous decision-making. This suggests safety validation for AI-driven humanoids is immature and that existing standards leave gaps.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: One abstract. The 30 risk scenarios are an analytical exercise, not field incident data, so the findings show where risk may sit, not how often failures occur. The authors also say their framework 'bridges the gap' with existing standards, which implies a gap exists. No independent validation is visible in the abstract.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Applying this framework to 30 risk scenarios revealed critical vulnerabilities, including power system malfunctions, software logic errors, and autonomous decision anomalies.

findings.claim: Autonomous humanoid manipulation skills are still narrow and mostly shown in controlled settings. A recent method reports a 70% success rate in unseen environments, so roughly 3 in 10 attempts are not reported as successful.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The abstract itself says current approaches rely on teleoperation or sim-to-real RL and that demonstrated skills are limited. Its own result covers five tasks. The 70% figure is the authors' headline result, and whether it is sufficient for commercial use is my inference, not a claim in the paper. It is an arXiv-style preprint and is not peer reviewed. Task count and trial counts are not visible in the abstract.
findings.supporting_excerpt: demonstrated autonomous skills remain limited and are typically restricted to controlled environments.

findings.claim: Early construction-site humanoid work shows only modest evidence: eight actions learned from demonstrations, with an average pose-tracking error of about 82 mm. The authors call it an early step, and the paper notes limited prior research on practical construction capability.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Single abstract, arXiv preprint (not peer reviewed). The abstract does not say whether tests were run on a real construction site, how many trials were run, or how an 82 mm error compares with the tolerance construction work needs. Those are gaps, not shown failures.
findings.supporting_excerpt: This work provides an early step toward deploying humanoid collaborators in construction.

findings.claim: Impressive humanoid demonstrations may be built on stacked, loosely integrated architectures (VLA models, teleoperation priors, control, safety wrappers) and not on unified general-purpose intelligence. Cited weaknesses include distribution shift, affordance grounding errors and teleoperation overfitting.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_7c9ec894f4 is a Zenodo preprint with a theoretical, categorical framing. It is not peer reviewed and the abstract is truncated, so its empirical grounding is unclear. src_cb51966cee (ACM Computing Surveys) separately says current humanoids remain 'distant from achieving human-like intelligence'. The two sources agree in direction, but the first is argument rather than measurement.

findings.claim: Teleoperation, a main route to humanoid data and capability, is hard in unstructured environments with limited communication. Robot-free demonstration collection is being proposed because teleoperation is logistically hard. This points to a data-collection bottleneck.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The survey (IEEE T-RO, 2023, widely cited) states the teleoperation challenge. The HuMI preprint (not peer reviewed) says teleoperation and sim-to-real RL are hindered by hardware logistics and reward engineering. Combining them into a 'data bottleneck' is my synthesis. The survey dates from 2023, so newer progress may not be reflected.
findings.supporting_excerpt: However, the complexity of humanoid robots imposes challenges for teleoperation, particularly in unstructured dynamic environments with limited communication.

findings.claim: Cybersecurity and sensing integrity are open risks. Instruction authentication does not confirm what a humanoid physically does, and motor-sensor observations can themselves be unreliable. A proposed fix has so far been tested on an educational robot.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: One preprint, not peer reviewed, with a truncated abstract. It names the Booster Robotics K1 Education humanoid as the test platform, so generalization to full-size industrial humanoids is untested here. The proposed framework is only one candidate mitigation, and there is no evidence yet on real-world attack rates.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Traditional instruction authentication mainly protects the instruction itself and cannot directly verify the final physical action of the robot.

findings.claim: Long-term reliability and maintenance evidence for humanoids is thin. Reliability modelling of interacting failure modes is described as challenging, and the reported fault-prediction and maintenance demonstrations use one humanoid system or two research robots.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_58015b75ea states that dependent competing failure modelling 'remains challenging' and shows feasibility on a single humanoid system. src_42602f3333 reports a 10-minute lead time on GUCnoid 1.0 and ARAtronica. Neither abstract reports fleet-scale, multi-year field failure data, so the absence of such data is a gap, not proof of poor reliability. The 10-minute lead time is also short for maintenance planning.

findings.claim: Contact with the environment is a documented structural and failure-mode concern for humanoids, and a 2026 safety-systems paper covers emergency stop, collision detection and safe failure modes. The abstracts available are empty or title-only, so no conclusions can be drawn.
findings.label: unverified_claim
findings.rationale: src_169c787a16 has metadata only and src_43840c18c0 has only a title-like abstract (a Zenodo preprint). Their existence indicates attention to failure modes and fail-safe design, but their findings are unknown to me.

findings.claim: A working paper asserts that humanoid motion control is an openly unsolved problem, with failure modes such as sensor-fusion degradation, model-DOF mismatch and feedback bandwidth limits. The paper is a conceptual diagnostic, not an empirical study.
findings.label: unverified_claim
findings.rationale: Zenodo working paper, not peer reviewed. It discloses LLM assistance, proposes no algorithms and offers no data. Its listed engineering challenges are plausible but are not independently supported by other papers in this set.

hype_flags: 'Appearance of general purpose physical intelligence': the Zenodo preprint argues such systems are stacked architectures, not unified agents
Humanoid 'collaborators' in construction: evidence is eight actions and an early-stage preprint
Humanoid 'advisers, educators, medical professionals, caregivers': the review itself admits current humanoids are far from human-like intelligence
'Significantly enhances traditional risk assessments': the abstract shows no baseline comparison or independent validation
Framings such as 'Industry-10.0' and the EOS 'coherence triad': conceptual, with no empirical evidence in the abstracts
Success rates from small task sets (e.g. five tasks) presented as general whole-body manipulation capability

finding.claim: S1 and S2 are presented as complementary, but they point in different directions on a central design question. Exbody says direct imitation of human motion capture fails on a real humanoid and so stops imitating the legs. The Adam paper claims human-locomotion imitation works for a full-size humanoid, including locomotion. The findings do not reconcile this. The difference may come from hardware design, the adversarial-prior method or evaluation scope. As written, S1's "must be relaxed" reads as a general rule that S2 appears to contradict. Also, S1's headline "human-like whole-body control" is only upper-body imitation, because the legs follow a velocity command.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The two abstracts give opposite framings of leg imitation. Only abstracts were read, so the cause of the difference cannot be determined. The Science agent should have flagged the tension instead of presenting both as a coherent trend.
finding.supporting_excerpt: directly performing imitation learning with the motion capture dataset would not work on the real humanoid robot, given the large gap in degrees of freedom and physical capabilities.

finding.claim: S2 repeats the authors' self-assessment ("human-comparable performance") as a verified fact. It rests on a single arXiv preprint with no citation count. The abstract gives no metric, baseline or hardware evaluation protocol that would show what 'human-comparable' means. The same abstract mixes the performance claim with a novel-hardware claim, so it is unclear how much of the result comes from the algorithm and how much from Adam's bespoke design. A 'verified_fact' label with medium confidence overstates what a self-reported abstract can establish.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The quoted text is the authors' own promotional claim. The abstract says the structural design 'greatly improves the efficiency and effectiveness of the imitation learning process', so the result is confounded with custom hardware and is not independently validated.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Adam can exhibit unprecedented human-like characteristics in locomotion tasks.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S3 credits all three cited papers with sim-to-real transfer on socially visible tasks (stylised walking, handshaking, dancing). Only the Exbody abstract states these demonstrations. The Adam abstract does not mention these tasks or an explicit sim-to-real transfer. iWalker is a vision-based walking and obstacle-avoidance system. The finding therefore overgeneralises one paper's results to a broader trend.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The excerpt comes from the Exbody abstract only. The other two cited abstracts do not contain handshaking or dancing. The claim is supported for one paper, not for the three attributed.
finding.supporting_excerpt: our policy can control a humanoid robot to walk in different styles, shake hands with humans, and even dance with a human in the real world.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S6's 'two-layer stack' synthesis is not what the cited papers show, and it is partly contradicted by them. GR00T N1 is described as two tightly coupled modules trained jointly end-to-end. iWalker is motivated by replacing modular pipelines with an end-to-end sense-plan-act system. MASH has no human motion prior and is about limb-level multi-agent RL. Only Trinity plausibly fits a modular RL-plus-LLM split. R4 also suggests such stacks may be loosely integrated rather than a clean architecture. The finding presents a convergent design pattern that the evidence does not demonstrate.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: This is the Science agent's own synthesis and it is labelled as interpretation, but it cites papers that argue for end-to-end or non-hierarchical designs. The trend toward a two-layer stack is therefore weaker than stated.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Both modules are tightly coupled and jointly trained end-to-end.

finding.claim: S8 reports MASH's gains (faster convergence, better whole-body cooperation) with no caveat. The abstract mentions no real-robot validation, no named baselines and no magnitude of improvement. The source is a single preprint with no citation record. The evidence should be treated as probably simulation-level and not yet confirmed on hardware.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstract never mentions hardware or quantifies the improvement. Its absence is an inference from the abstract only. The full paper may contain these details.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Experiments demonstrate that MASH accelerates training convergence and improves whole-body cooperation ability, outperforming conventional single-agent reinforcement learning methods.

finding.claim: The findings on whole-body control and sim-to-real (S1-S3, S6) show capability demonstrations but omit reliability and robustness evidence. The risk search found that autonomous humanoid skills are still limited and mostly confined to controlled environments, and that a recent method reaches 70% success in unseen environments. The findings also leave out that safety validation for AI-driven humanoids is described as immature. Without these caveats, the demonstrations read as nearer to deployable than the evidence supports.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The quote is from the HuMI abstract. The 70% unseen-environment success rate is also in that abstract. These risk-side findings counterbalance success-focused demonstrations that report no failure rates.
finding.supporting_excerpt: demonstrated autonomous skills remain limited and are typically restricted to controlled environments.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S13 says 'the papers argue', but one paper is cited. That paper's supporting evidence is simulation-only and built around a single Tesla Optimus case. Its claim that humanoids compete with robotic arms and need ROI methods is a statement of need, not a finding. The finding also omits that its only empirical result is a simulated lean-assembly cell.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The excerpt shows the manufacturing evidence is simulated. The plural 'papers' is not supported by the single cited source.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Simulation results indicate that humanoids can increase the level of manufacturing automation.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

limitations: Only 12 papers, judged on titles and abstracts, and some abstracts are empty, truncated or title-only (src_169c787a16, src_43840c18c0, src_f1c3de13cb, src_7c9ec894f4).
Many sources are non-peer-reviewed preprints (arXiv, Zenodo), and several have zero citations.

The set has no hardware-economics evidence: no actuator cost, battery energy density or runtime, thermal limits, supply-chain concentration or unit-economics data. These are gaps in the search, not evidence that no problems exist.
No company-specific or deployment-scale evidence is present, so commercial claims cannot be assessed.
The risk-oriented search returned mostly framework and modelling papers, so the failure rates and safety record of real deployed humanoids are not covered.
Possible alternatives that could displace humanoids (wheeled or task-specific robots) are not addressed by any paper provided.
Only titles and abstracts were available, so claims that appear to be missing from an abstract may be present in the full paper.
Most cited Science papers are preprints, and many have no citation counts. I could not check independent replication or peer review.
Some risk-search evidence is itself weak: Zenodo working papers, a conceptual diagnostic, and title-only entries. I gave it little weight.
I left S4, S5, S7, S9, S10, S11 and S12 unchallenged. They describe what the abstracts state, and their low or medium confidence fits that.

sources.title: CLUTCH FOR AN ACTUATOR FOR A HUMANOID ROBOT [US20260348439A1]
sources.abstract: A torque protection apparatus for a humanoid robot actuator protects a high-reduction strain wave gearbox from damage caused by transient overload torque. The apparatus is arranged co-axially with the gearbox and includes an output ring, formed by the circular spline of the strain wave gearbox, having opposed planar disc surfaces that are axially clamped between first and second clutch friction plates. An outer body surrounds the gearbox and connects to an output adaptor, while an inner body within the outer body bounds a sealed annular hydraulic chamber holding a captive incompressible liquid. A hydraulic adjustment piston pressurizes the liquid, biasing the inner body axially against the friction plates and output ring to set a threshold breakaway torque. Below the threshold, the friction plates transmit full gearbox torque to the output adaptor.

sources.title: FOOT-LOCAL PREDICTIVE CONTACT VALIDATION FOR HUMANOID ROBOT LOCOMOTION [US20260349434A1]
sources.abstract: A humanoid robot system includes a locomotion controller, robotic foot assembly, foot-local predictive contact validator, and footfall-release controller. A candidate footfall command is received for the robotic foot assembly. Before weight transfer or lower-body actuator execution, the foot-local predictive contact validator evaluates local foot state, terrain state, and body-state context to predict a contact consequence associated with the candidate footfall command. The predicted contact consequence may include slip risk, toe overhang, terrain-compliance mismatch, insufficient contact area, ankle torque overload, or unsafe load transfer. The footfall-release controller evaluates the predicted contact consequence against a footfall-safety policy and selectively releases, modifies, delays, or blocks the candidate footfall command. In some embodiments, a release authorization defines a validator-derived support envelope enforced by one or more downstream actuator controllers.

sources.title: HUMANOID-NATIVE PREDICTIVE ACTUATION VALIDATION USING WHOLE-BODY RUNTIME STATE [US20260346448A1]
sources.abstract: A humanoid robot intercepts a candidate humanoid action before actuator-command dispatch and obtains whole-body runtime state including body configuration and a support, contact, environment, object, human-relative, or actuator state. A predictive actuation validator predicts future physical consequences of executing the candidate action over an action-dependent prediction horizon and evaluates the consequences against humanoid-native criteria including stability, support contact, self-collision, human clearance, actuator limits, terrain contact, or object retention. The validator may dynamically select or configure a forward-looking evaluator according to participating body regions, support phase, contact schedule, payload, uncertainty, or risk. More than one evaluator type may predict different consequence classes for a common action. A release decision releases, modifies, stages, decomposes, reroutes, or rejects the action. Motion of one body region may be validated based on a predicted consequence at another body region, enabling whole-body, cross-region predictive evaluation before physical execution.

sources.title: PRIVACY PRESERVING EDGE-CLOUD COLLABORATION FOR EMBODIED AI AGENTS [US20260349798A1]

sources.title: Cobotic System for Intraoperative Data Collection and Predictive Analytics [US20260346454A1]
sources.abstract: A perioperative humanoid cobot system includes a robotic platform configured to autonomously support surgical teams through integrated vision, communication, and documentation capabilities. The system comprises a humanoid robotic body with articulated arms and a head-mounted stereoscopic vision system capable of optical, thermal, and depth imaging. A control system coordinates autonomous navigation, personnel and object recognition, sterile field compliance, and intraoperative data acquisition. A multimodal communication interface supports real-time telepresence, enabling remote participants to interact with surgical staff through audio, video, and augmented or virtual reality interfaces. The system further includes a data recording module configured to capture and log timestamped surgical activity, instrument usage, and personnel movements to cloud-based storage for postoperative analysis. Modular components, including swappable sensor payloads and configurable display systems, allow the cobot to adapt to varied surgical workflows while maintaining safe and sterile operation.

sources.title: Perioperative Cobotic System with Bimodal Conveyance [US20260346423A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A perioperative humanoid cobot is disclosed having bimodal locomotion for autonomous operation in surgical environments. The system includes articulated legs with integrated wheels enabling transitions between bipedal walking and wheeled rolling modes without external reconfiguration. A control system with an intelligence module fuses perception data from cameras, LiDAR, and force sensors to map surroundings, plan paths, and select locomotion mode based on terrain and task context. The cobot can step over obstacles, roll efficiently along corridors, or dock with a powered platform for extended range. Redundant sensing, geofencing, and fail-safe controls ensure safe operation near staff and sterile zones. Equipped with robotic arms and end effectors, the cobot performs transport, positioning, and perioperative support tasks under supervised or autonomous control, improving efficiency, safety, and workflow integration in hospital settings.

sources.title: Perioperative Cobotic System with Multiple Imaging Modalities for Environmental Awareness [US20260351381A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A perioperative cobotic system is disclosed for intraoperative environmental awareness and task execution. The system includes a humanoid mobile cobot equipped with a multi-modal imaging suite comprising RGB cameras, depth sensors, thermal imagers, and panoramic lenses. Sensor data are fused to generate a unified, real-time spatial map of the operating room, including dynamic personnel, equipment, and sterile field boundaries. A surgical phase detection engine applies machine learning to infer procedural stages from visual patterns. A context-aware task execution system triggers cobot actions aligned with surgical workflow events, while a human interaction interface supports gesture and voice-based commands. The system adapts to lighting changes and occlusions using redundant sensing and dynamic fusion logic. Logged imaging and system data support real-time visualization and postoperative review. Safety and privacy controls enforce sterile field compliance and data access restrictions. The system enables autonomous, responsive support for surgical teams during complex intraoperative procedures.

sources.title: ACTIVE DISTURBANCE REJECTION CONTROL METHOD FOR LINEAR ELECTRIC-DRIVEN JOINT OF HUMANOID ROBOT [US20260336101A1]
authors: HANGZHOU SEENPIN ELECTROMECHANICAL TRANS CO LTD
sources.organization: HANGZHOU SEENPIN ELECTROMECHANICAL TRANS CO LTD
sources.abstract: [0000]    The present invention discloses an active disturbance rejection control method for a linear electric-driven joint of a humanoid robot, and the method includes: establishing a dynamic model for a linear electric-driven joint system used in the humanoid robot; determining an extended state observer based on the dynamic model, estimating a state variable and an unknown disturbance of the system in real time, and dynamically compensating for the disturbance through the extended state observer; determining a nonlinear feedback control law based on states and estimated disturbance information observed by the extended state observer; and analyzing stability of the extended state observer and the nonlinear feedback control law, and adjusting parameters of the extended state observer and the nonlinear feedback control law based on analysis results. For the active disturbance rejection control method for a linear electric-driven joint of a humanoid robot according to the present invention, an active disturbance rejection control technology is adopted to overcome limitations of conventional PID control in a nonlinear and uncertain system, efficiently controlling the linear electric-driven joint, thereby enhancing dynamic performance and robustness of the humanoid robot.

sources.title: HUMANOID ROBOT DATA COLLECTION SYSTEM HAVING VIRTUAL REALITY DISPLAYS [US20260339321A1]
sources.abstract: A portable data collection system for capturing operator movement data to control or train a humanoid robot. The system includes a wearable apparatus, such as a base mount with an adjustable back harness, supporting first and second articulated arms pivotably coupled thereto. Each articulated arm comprises rigid frame links connected by joints instrumented with joint encoders. Gloves coupled to distal portions of the arms include hand sensors measuring finger movement. A head-mounted display presents visual feedback from the robot. A piloting control system, communicatively coupled to the encoders and hand sensors, generates control data and selectively suspends and resumes its generation or transmission—for example, upon detecting operator movement outside a defined task workspace or velocity profile, and upon detecting a predetermined resumption gesture, actuation, or voice command. A shared time synchronization clock enables timestamped logging of sensor measurements paired with robot-state records, supporting consistent operator-side and robot-side signal characteristics.

sources.title: META-CONTROL TECHNIQUES FOR HUMANOID ROBOT DATA COLLECTION SYSTEM [US20260336123A1]
sources.abstract: A robot teleoperation system and methods enable a human operator to issue meta-commands to a robot while a primary motion-mapping interface continuously maps the operator's limb movement to the robot. Meta-commands are received through non-primary input modalities—including voice, gaze, foot pedals, or anatomically distinct gestures lying outside the robot's kinematic envelope—and modify operational state without interrupting primary motion mapping. Meta-commands include toggling a data collection subsystem for machine learning training, adjusting a posture parameter of the robot, engaging a clutch to suspend mapping while maintaining a commanded pose, or causing the robot to perform a predetermined motion. A clutch-gated channel further permits re-origination of a tracking origin, fine adjustment of joint angles or end-effector coordinates, and state toggles received via an independent modality while the robot holds pose, after which motion mapping resumes through a velocity-limited blend.

sources.title: MOVEMENT SYSTEM, METHOD FOR CONTROLLING HUMANOID ROBOT, AND PROGRAM [WO2026221128A1]
sources.abstract: A movement system according to an embodiment of the present invention comprises: a humanoid robot that can ride an electric skateboard and an electric motorcycle and can travel autonomously; and a control unit that sets a to-be-ridden machine to be ridden by the humanoid robot to the electric skateboard or the electric motorcycle in accordance with movement instruction information pertaining to the humanoid robot, and causes the humanoid robot to ride the electric skateboard or the electric motorcycle that has been set.

sources.title: METHOD AND SYSTEM FOR CONSTRUCTING DENSE POINT CLOUD MAP FOR HUMANOID ROBOT [US20260330680A1]
sources.abstract: The invention provides a method and a system for constructing a dense point cloud map for a humanoid robot. The method includes: obtaining, in real time, a video image acquired during walking of the humanoid robot; determining a gait phase of the humanoid robot in a current frame image; estimating a camera pose of the current frame image based on the gait phase of the humanoid robot in the current frame image; determining whether the current frame image is a key frame based on the camera pose of the current frame image; and performing local mapping and loop closure detection by the key frame to obtain a global dense point cloud map. The invention effectively alleviates the blurring and jitter of the acquired data during mapping of the humanoid robot, such that a more accurate environmental map can be obtained, the precision of operational tasks of the robot is improved.

sources.abstract: The present invention provides a humanoid hand system for sterilizing an object, the humanoid hand system comprising: a UVC module mounted on the palm of a humanoid robot; a transparent protective cover for protecting the UVC module from the outside; a sensor for detecting a user; and a control unit electrically connected to the humanoid robot, the UVC module, and the sensor, wherein the control unit controls the UVC module on the basis of detection by the sensor.

authors: OVERSONIC ROBOTICS S R L SOC BENEFIT
sources.organization: OVERSONIC ROBOTICS S R L SOC BENEFIT
sources.abstract: It is herein described an operator and transporter humanoid robot (1) comprising a robotic torso (2), at least two robotic arms (3) connected sideways to the robotic torso (2) opposite each other, at least one support column (11) for the robotic torso (2) and a navigation and transport base defined between a front end (13) and a rear end (14). The support column (11) is fitted close to the front end (13) of the base (12) and the navigation and transport base comprises a transport plate (15) comprising transport elements in a substantially central position between the front end (13) and the rear end (14) or close to the rear end (14) of the base (12). The support column (11) and the transport plate (15) are adapted to rotate about an axis that is transversal to the navigation and transport base in a coordinated and counter-rotating and/or selective manner.

sources.title: STRUCTURE FOR ANIMATED HUMANOID PROP [US20260325988A1]
sources.abstract: An exemplary humanoid prop includes a plurality of rods configured to be coupled together and including two arm rods and two leg rods. The prop further includes a plurality of plates configured to be coupled to the plurality of rods such that the plurality of plates and the plurality of rods resemble a human body when coupled together and placed in a costume.

sources.title: SPATIALLY COLLABORATIVE TELEASSISTANCE OR TELEOPERATION SESSIONS FOR PHYSICAL AI DEPLOYED IN REAL WORLD ENVIRONMENTS DURING TRAINING AND OPERATIONS [US20260330208A1]
sources.abstract: [0000] Spatially collaborative teleassistance and teleoperation of a physical AI unit (e.g., a humanoid robot or autonomous vehicle) deployed in a real-world environment. The system utilizes a remote AI control node comprising an AI agent, such as a Large Language Model (LLM) or Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system, communicatively coupled to the physical AI unit via a data network. A prompt enhancement engine converts multi-modal sensor data—including visual, acoustic, and haptic inputs from the physical AI's environment—into semantic text tokens that are injected into a structured system prompt. This allows the remote AI agent to generate context-aware training scenarios and remotely control the on-site unit by issuing simulated human commands that mimic human controls, such as synthetic voice, simulated joystick movements, and simulated iris gaze data. The architecture integrates robotics simulation and physics engines (e.g., NVIDIA Isaac and Cosmos) to ground the AI agent's logic in reality, enabling a hybrid operation mode that bridges the gap between simulation and real-world deployment (Sim2Real) through real-time, multi-modal feedback lo

sources.title: HUMANOID TECHNICAL SYSTEM FOR PREDICTING AND STIMULATING HUMAN EMOTIONAL REACTIONS DURING INTERVIEW [UA164612U]
sources.abstract: Humanoid technical system for predicting and stimulating human emotional reactions during interview includes a speech module and a built-in computing module. The system is designed as a housing shaped like a human body, comprising a head with a face, a neck, shoulders, a torso, and limbs. The facial expression system includes a set of electromechanical actuators with a resolution of at least 0.5°, mounted beneath a layer of artificial facial skin, as well as video cameras based on CMOS sensors with a resolution of at least 1080p and a frame rate of at least 30 frames per second. The microphones have a sensitivity of at least –40 dB and a frequency range of 20–20,000 Hz. The speakers have a frequency range of 80–8,000 Hz, are installed in the head region, and are connected to the speech module. The inertial sensors consist of three-axis accelerometers and gyroscopes located in the neck and shoulder regions. The computing module contains a multi-core processor with a neural network trained using methods from evaluation theory, affective control theory, and statement reliability analysis. The computing module is designed to process multimodal data obtained from video cameras, microphones, and inertial sensors, and to generate control signals for reproducing facial, vocal, and behavioral responses in real time.

sources.title: PROPRIOCEPTION SYSTEM FOR A HUMANOID ROBOT [US20260316292A1]
sources.abstract: A method and system for determining the position and orientation of parts and components of a humanoid robot using a body self-perception model (BSPM). The BSPM executes on onboard processors and receives image data from cameras mounted in the robot's head and on or near its hands. The BSPM processes the image data to detect and localize keypoints on the robot's own components and determines six-degree-of-freedom poses therefrom. The determined poses are provided to an onboard AI system that generates motor commands in a closed-loop control cycle. The BSPM may dynamically weight keypoint-based and holistic pose estimation based on occlusion degree, express poses using a delta SE(3) representation, and output uncertainty estimates that modulate control behavior. The system may fuse camera data with data from inertial measurement units, joint encoders, or other sensor modalities to produce position estimates exceeding the accuracy achievable by any single sensor alone.

sources.title: Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Based Dexterous Manipulation on Humanoids [US20260316276A1]
sources.abstract: Mechanisms for configuring a humanoid robot comprising a plurality of multi-fingered graspers to perform dexterous manipulation tasks, whereby a plurality of simulated environments are generated representing a distribution of kinematic parameter combinations corresponding to a physical robot. In each simulated environment, a target trajectory sequence recorded from the physical robot is executed. For each simulated environment, a tracking error relative to execution of the target trajectory sequence by the physical robot is calculated. One or more simulated environments are selected based on a minimization of an average squared difference between simulated tracking error and real-world tracking error, and a manipulation policy for the physical robot is then trained within the selected simulated environments using reinforcement learning.

sources.title: Elbow assembly of a humanoid robot [US12759173B1]
sources.abstract: A humanoid robot comprises a torso and an arm assembly with an upper arm twist actuator, lower humerus, upper forearm, and elbow actuator. The lower humerus features a humerus extender coupled to the twist actuator and an elbow actuator mating assembly with a curvilinear external surface. The upper forearm includes a coupling assembly with a U-shaped external surface in a first plane, and an extender with a U-shaped external surface in a second plane perpendicular to the first plane. The elbow actuator has one extent received within the mating assembly and another extent within the coupling assembly, with these assemblies collectively surrounding most of the elbow actuator. This configuration enables controlled arm movement while maintaining structural integrity at the elbow joint.

draft.summary: Research and patent activity on humanoid robots is rising fast. Papers grew 54.3% from 2024 to 2025 and 60.7% in 2026 year to date, and patent publications grew 121.6% from 2024 to 2025 and 56.4% year to date [S1, S4, P1, P4]. Company filings show real commercial intent: Tesla is preparing large-scale Optimus production, Mobileye acquired Mentee Robotics, and Richtech and Faraday Future report early humanoid products [M1, M2, M4, M5]. The evidence for reliable, deployable capability is much weaker. Autonomous skills are narrow and mostly shown in controlled settings, one method reaches 70% success in unseen environments, safety validation is immature, and the Risk challenges show that several Science findings overstate their sources [R1, R2, R3, C1, C2, C3, C4, C6]. Customer adoption evidence is mostly social-media signals or early-stage filings, and Mobileye itself warns the industry may not develop as expected [M8, X4]. The main uncertainty is whether simulation-trained control and foundation models can become reliable enough, at an acceptable cost, to turn demonstrations into paid deployments. Research and patent counts are not evidence of commercial success.
draft.plain_summary: Humanoid robots are human-shaped machines meant to do physical work. Scientists, patent filers and some big companies are putting rapidly growing effort into them. But the evidence that they work reliably outside controlled settings, or that many customers are paying for them, is still thin. The biggest thing that could stop progress is that today's robots still fail too often and the safety rules are not mature.
